data.description: You’ll leave fed, challenged and gastronomically punch-drunk Nico Simeone is the Scottish-Italian chef behind the Six by Nico restaurant empire, and Lennox, in Spring Gardens, Manchester, is his new baby. If you are unfamiliar with Six by Nico, it’s a fever-dream version of fine dining: Simeone conjured up themes such as “The Chippie”, “ Italian Road Trip ” and “ Ancient Rome ”, then served six courses in homage to them. Tokyo! Mad Hatters! Childhood! At one point, the Six empire was growing like knotweed, and by 2025 there were 17 restaurants. You had more chance of eating at a Six by Nico than finding an NHS dentist. Suffice to say, many adore the concept – overlooking its middling cooking skills – because it’s pocket-friendly, and the six-course format gives a night out with friends a sense of occasion not available at Pizza Express. Lennox, Simeone says, will be very different: à la carte, focused on dry-aged meat, but with the same playfulness and invention. There would be a fish finger with katsu curry and celeriac remoulade; a tempura oyster shell filled with dry-aged beef tartare and oyster emulsion; and gnocchi with deboned chicken wings and parmesan. Lennox would be personal, bespoke and absolutely unscalable. No rollout planned, no siree. But by August 2026, there will be three of them. Hang on, what? Yes, shortly after Manchester came Glasgow, and then Edinburgh. Simeone sleeps with one eye open; I salute his indefatigability. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Everywhere there were pitifully injured people’: how a newly unearthed memoir captures the devastation of Hiroshima
data.description: In an exclusive extract from his memoir, Kiyoshi Tanimoto describes the terrifying trip across the city to locate his wife and child • ‘I didn’t want to be a victim of the bomb’: read an interview with Tanimoto’s daughter Koko Kondo Most of the people of Hiroshima had neither seen nor heard any plane. They heard no sound of explosion. They had seen only a strange flash in open daylight, or merely felt the reflection of the flash. However, there had been a tremendous explosion. The parents of Mr Konda, one of our church members, had been waiting for a train at Yokogawa station, located 2km [one and a quarter miles] away from the centre of the bomb’s explosion. They saw a B-29 and a parachute dropping through the air. Before they had time to wonder at the sight, they fell unconscious. Afterward, they could not remember sensing any sound or light. When they regained consciousness, they found themselves lying on the ground, burned and without any clothing. The houses all around had been crushed to the ground. After getting to their feet, they ran toward the suburbs. Other people rushing along the Koi highway had the same experience. Continue reading...

data.title: The AI jobs apocalypse probably isn’t coming anytime soon
data.description: Artificial intelligence  may not deliver on its promise of vast economic opportunity at a price that humanity is willing to pay In March, Anthropic, the cutting-edge artificial intelligence business that gave us the chatbot Claude, published an analysis on the impact of AI on employment, to help us assess the claim that intelligent robots were about to redefine human existence, ending demand for human labor. Last year in May, Anthropic’s co-founder, Dario Amodei, claimed AI could wipe out half of all entry-level jobs in one to five years. Last January, he told us AI would probably become a “general labor substitute for humans”. In June he said we risk “a world where the economic trade-off dial is stuck on the hypergrowth, hyper-inequality setting”. Continue reading...

data.title: Revealed: history of Spain’s fearless 1970s trans-rights political collective
data.description: Pioneering activists risked arrest and imprisonment amid lingering persecution after Franco dictatorship New research has shed light on Spain’s first transgender political organisation, a trailblazing collective that was launched in 1978 as its members grappled with the lingering persecution of the country’s four-decade dictatorship. Founded in Barcelona, the Colectivo de Travestis y Transexuales, or Collective of Transvestis and Transexuals, sought to add its voice to the heated conversation playing out across Spain in the transition to democracy after the death of the dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Continue reading...

data.title: Beaten, robbed and driven out: violent demonstrations target immigrants in South Africa
data.description: Thousands have fled amid months of anti-immigration protests as campaigners demand undocumented people leave the country In Thembelihle, an informal settlement south of Johannesburg where thousands of breeze-block houses and metal shacks line dirt streets flooded with filthy water, Malawians had lived for years alongside South Africans without any problems. But in the last few weeks, a series of armed robberies has shaken the community. On 29 June, several men broke into the compound of Eibraheem Hussein, a 60-year-old Malawian who has lived in South Africa since 2000. They beat him and stole valuable items. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Iran accuses Kyiv of deadly attack on Iranian vessel in Caspian Sea
data.description: Zelenskyy says Iran is using Russian satellite images to help direct strikes in Middle East. What we know on day 1,614 Iran’s foreign ministry on Saturday condemned what it called a ⁠Ukrainian attack on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea , saying it killed one sailor and ⁠injured another. Tehran called the apparent attack an act of aggression and said it would defend its national ​interests and security. Ukraine’s diplomatic representative to Iran was summoned, Iranian state media reported. Throughout ​the war in Ukraine, Kyiv has had to counter Iranian-designed drones deployed by Moscow, and it has offered its drone ⁠interception expertise to countries in the Middle East that have been attacked by Iran. Iran and Russia are two of the five countries that border the Caspian Sea and Russia maintains a powerful naval force there , making the inland body of water a platform for long‑range power projection , and a vital strategic bridge to Iran. Iran’s denunciation of the Ukraine attack on the ship coincided with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s comments that Russia was passing its satellite observations in the Middle East to Iran to enable it ‌to direct strikes in the region. Zelenskyy on Saturday said on X that Ukraine had “achieved very strong results with long‑range strikes in the Caspian Sea – including vessels used in military cargo shipments involving Iran”. Zelenskyy also said Russia wanted to bring ⁠in 30,000 ⁠North Korean ​troops to take part in its more than four-year-old conflict with Russia, and was ⁠already preparing to receive them. Under a mutual defence pact, North Korea sent an ⁠estimated 14,000 soldiers to Russia’s Kursk Region in ​2024 to help ‌Moscow beat back ‌a major incursion into the region by Ukrainian ‌forces. “Preparations have been under way in Russia’s ‌Voronezh region since June to receive [North Korean troops],” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address, adding that the communist dictatorship was preparing ​to supply Russia with new launchers for ballistic missiles. Twelve people were killed, including five children, in an drone attack ⁠on ​a holiday camp in a Russian-held part of Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region , Russian-installed local authorities said on Saturday, ⁠accusing Ukraine of deliberately attacking civilians. Kyiv did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Meanwhile, the ⁠Ukrainian capital Kyiv came under attack from Russian forces ⁠early on ⁠Sunday, ​with falling debris triggering fires in at least three ⁠districts, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Ukraine’s air force said Russian ⁠forces had targeted the capital with ​ballistic missiles. ‌But an ‌air alert was lifted after about ‌50 minutes and the air force rescinded its warning of missile deployment. Klitschko said one blaze had broken out on the seventh ‌and eighth floors of a multi-storey apartment block in ​a central district. There were no immediate ⁠reports of casualties. Kazakhstan’s ⁠president, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, said on Saturday a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine might be ⁠reached if ⁠both sides froze the conflict and resumed negotiations . Tokayev made the remarks while meeting Vladimir Putin at a Russia-Kazakhstan forum ⁠in the Siberian city of Omsk. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, quoted by the state ​TASS news agency, said Putin outlined to Tokayev in detail the state of Russia’s military operations in Ukraine. Continue reading...

data.title: How to keep cool in a heatwave: 25 tips from the people who know best, from a Rio lifeguard to an Egyptian archaeologist
data.description: For some, scorching days and humid nights are just the norm. So how do they stay chilled and comfortable? Luis Pacherrez Antón is president of Agroperu Cooperative, a democratic collective of 102 small-scale farmers in the Chira River valley, Peru. He is based in Piura, known as “the city of eternal heat” because it stays hot and dry all year round. “The sun rays start to shine very early – from 9am,” he says. “So as people who work in cultivation, under a burning sun, we stay comfortable by starting much earlier and consuming the healthy foods that we produce, like bananas, oranges, lemons, grapes, papayas and avocados.” Continue reading...

data.title: What makes a woman a witch? Financial independence
data.description: Women aren’t being burnt at the stake any more, but there is still risk and violence implicit in the label ‘witch’ When Katherine Harrison’s husband passed away, she became the wealthiest woman in Wethersfield, Connecticut. Rather than wallow in her new status as a young widow she decided to run the farm she’d inherited on her own. She took up ranching and a slew of other hobbies including brewing ale, spinning yarn and beekeeping. She traded honey and beeswax for candles. She was by all accounts, headstrong, outspoken and clever. In many corners of the internet, Harrison’s interests are having a moment. Craft brewers have been spruiking classic ales for years, urban beekeeping is surging in popularity, and people are looking to textile-based crafts as ways to practise mindfulness. data.title: Romantasy star Stacey McEwan: ‘You’re not going to recommend Fifty Shades of Grey to your Catholic grandma’
data.description: The author and BookTok luminary on the nightmare trope, how to convert a straight man into loving fantasy romance, and words that should never be used in a sex scene What’s the weirdest thing you’ve ever done for love? I was working in a bakery on the Gold Coast and across the way was a Go Sushi, and I had a crush on the boy that worked there. I was about 16. We’d close at about the same time in the evening, and I would have to throw away all of the bread that we didn’t sell and he would have to throw away all the sushi. He would always finish first, so sometimes he’d come across and help me – not allowed, by the way. And I thought it would be really funny, on one such occasion, if I did a bit where I hollowed out a cob loaf and put it on my head and stacked loaves of bread up my arms, and I put Vienna loaves on my shoes and started skating around the floor calling myself Bread Girl, thinking that he’s obviously going to find this hilarious. He laughed along, then about five minutes later he asked me if he could have my older sister’s phone number. Continue reading...

data.title: Staff turnover is rampant under Trump 2.0 – with insidious results | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: A new report shows more Senate-confirmed staffers have left their jobs this time around than in his first term Donald Trump loves a construction project. He’s building a ballroom, revamping a reflecting pool, and overseeing the construction of a skyline-altering arch in Washington DC. For his next real estate scheme, may I suggest a giant revolving door in the White House? It would certainly get a lot of use: senior officials are leaving Trump’s second administration at record rates. According to a new report called Quiet Chaos by the nonpartisan Partnership for Public Service, 27 Senate-confirmed officials have left their positions within cabinet departments to date. That’s nearly 150% higher than the 11 departures in the first 18 months of Trump’s first administration. Per the report, it is also “nearly two and a half times as many as Trump’s first administration (11) and over six times as many as the average between the George W Bush, Barack Obama and Joe Biden administrations (4.3)”. Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The hill I will die on: Breakfast cereal is for babies – I eat salad in the mornings, like a grownup | Jacq Kelly
data.description: There’s no way I could get by on a bowl of Coco Pops – give me sliced tomatoes and cucumber every time I recently got into a row on X about the unlikely subject of salad. I want to acknowledge that arguing with strangers on social media is definitely for babies and I should know better by now, but I’m a work in progress. And so I mentioned that I had enjoyed how readily available salads had been at breakfast buffets while I had been travelling in Denmark and Sweden this year compared with the UK. Salad has been a part of my breakfast for about a decade now, and I think a lot of people would benefit from it. It’s a pretty easy way of getting a couple of portions of fruit and veg before you have even left the house. All hell broke loose. Salad for breakfast is “not normal in a northern European climate”, according to one agitated typer in a response to my post about its availability at breakfasts there. In one of the towns we visited, Luleå , we were just 100km south of the Arctic Circle and the sea was still frozen in April. The hotel had an excellent breakfast buffet – a rotating assortment of freshly prepared salad items with fruit that hadn’t even been poured from a can. Someone should alert the authorities. Jacq Kelly is a Toronto-based writer and disability rights campaigner Continue reading...

data.title: Warning: Australian politicians are importing the British right’s visions of doom | Jack Jacobs
data.description: Having met Nigel Farage, Rupert Lowe and Tommy Robinson, Pauline Hanson is deploying their rhetoric in a country with a very different history of immigration In a 1950 essay, the critic AA Phillips wrote of a “cultural cringe” in which insecure Australians looked to Britain for instruction. Today, some Australians are championing far-right British actors and importing their visions of doom to Australia. In June, the former Australian Liberal prime minister Tony Abbott spoke at the Alliance for Responsible Citizenship conference, which is organised around the idea of “renewing” western civilisation. “Sustained mass migration, especially from countries with quite different cultures,” said Abbott, “[is] the surest and swiftest way … to dilute and eventually to extinguish the Anglo-Celtic core culture and the Judeo-Christian foundational ethos (which is actually what attracts migrants to the Anglosphere).” Peta Credlin, his former chief of staff, now a Sky News Australia commentator, said : “You are a petri dish … [on] multiculturalism and radical Islam, you are where we don’t want to go.” Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: Pogacar set for Tour de France glory in shortened finale as Carapaz wins stage 20
data.description: Four-time victor holds huge lead after Alpe d’Huez Final stage to be shortened due to wildfires elsewhere Tadej Pogacar’s likely victory parade on the streets of Paris will come sooner on Sunday after the final stage of the Tour de France was shortened due to wildfires elsewhere in France. The stage will now be only 89km long and will start on the Champs-Élysées, where two laps of the avenue will be followed by the now traditional circuits of the Butte Montmartre. In a joint statement with the prefecture police, the Tour organiser, ASO, said: “The ministry of the interior has decided to redeploy a portion of the internal security forces initially mobilised for the final stage of the Tour de France, in order to reinforce the response efforts in the areas affected by the wildfires. ” Continue reading...

data.title: Liverpool start Iraola era in style to beat Sunderland but Gomez injury deepens defensive worries
data.description: Liverpool defeat Sunderland 4-2 in friendly in Nashville When Gomez went down, central defence formed by two teenagers The Andoni Iraola era at Liverpool opened with a victory over Sunderland in Nashville – and a deepening of concerns over the defensive options at his disposal. The sight of Joe Gomez hobbling off after 10 minutes of the new head coach’s first game and two teenagers forming a raw central defence partnership in his absence intensified the spotlight on a department in need of work. Liverpool had few issues at the other end of the pitch against Regis Le Bris’s side, resplendent in pink in Tennessee, where second half finishes from Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas delivered an ultimately comfortable win. data.title: Anthony Joshua knocked down twice but stops Kristian Prenga in round two
data.description: Briton on canvas inside 20 seconds and later in first Joshua recovers to blast out Albanian in second round Anthony Joshua cleared his final hurdle in the ring, before he fights Tyson Fury in November, but he was knocked down twice, shockingly, in the first round of his wild and chaotic bout with Kristian Prenga. In the early hours of Sunday morning in Jeddah, a devastating knockout in the second left Prenga crumpled in a heap on the canvas, wrapped up in the ropes, and rescued Joshua from humiliation. After the opening three minutes his extravaganza with Fury looked as if it was about to end in abject ruins but Joshua pulled himself out of a dark pit streaked with defeat to salvage his career – and his much-hyped fight with his British compatriot. This was a crazy firefight of a tune-up for Joshua, who was boxing for the first time since being injured in the car accident that took the lives of two of his closest friends, Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele, last December. Continue reading...

data.description: Ramsay-Peaty finishes third in 100m breaststroke ‘People who comment … you don’t know who I am’ Adam Ramsay-Peaty has never been someone to mask his feelings. But defeat has never sounded as emotional or as raw as this. There were tears. Frustrations. Questions about why he kept putting himself through the 5.30am starts at the age of 31. And then came the crescendo in the form of a blistering attack on his critics on social media and the media. “You can’t hurt me,” he said, before telling them to “do better”. It was dramatic. It was powerful. And it was certainly heartfelt. Continue reading...

data.title: Former FDA official says US handling of cyclospora near ‘catastrophic level’
data.description: Frank Yiannas calls for an independent review of the federal response to the illness causing explosive diarrhea Donald Trump’s former top food safety official has accused the administration of a near “catastrophic” mismanagement of the cyclospora outbreak that has sickened thousands of people in the US. data.title: The Curse of Love Island review – the deaths are more complex than this documentary can handle
data.description: This show tries to grapple with the fact that three people associated with the reality juggernaut have killed themselves. But it forgets that the dating series doesn’t exist in a vacuum In summer 2015, ITV revived its 00s reality format Celebrity Love Island, a show that was remembered mostly as a drunken, downmarket rival to Big Brother. Its new, slick, civilian Love Island was a slow-burn at first, but by 2017 it was one of British TV’s biggest hits. While it remains among ITV’s hottest properties, viewing figures are now more modest, with 600,000 people tuning in for its 2026 launch. Tastes have changed, but the fact that three people associated with the show – former contestants Mike Thalassitis and Sophie Gradon, and Caroline Flack, the presenter for five series – took their lives, may also have made viewers wary. Timed to coincide with the finale of the latest series of Love Island on Monday, Prime Video has released this two-parter about the apparent “curse” that stalks the programme. It opens with former contestant Anton Danyluk, who appeared on the show in 2019, declaring that there is “no higher high than the summer you’re preparing for Love Island”. But a stint in the show’s Mallorcan villa proved less of a high for some. Luis Morrison – a 2015 Islander – says it feels “disgusting” and “embarrassing” to watch the show back. “Everyone was having sex and stuff,” he says. Malin Andersson, a 2016 contestant, says, looking back, the show feels “quite toxic … so superficial and artificial”. Watching footage of herself coming into the villa for a post-elimination row with her partner, Terry, Andersson alleges there was much meddling on the part of the programme-makers: “The producers are fucking with people who can feel deep things!” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘People who commit heinous crimes can be victims’: Michael Mann on the provocative power of Manhunter at 40
data.description: As a stunning 4K restoration arrives in theaters, the director and cast reflect on creating the disturbing descent into a criminal underworld Michael Mann has shown time and again in films like Thief , Heat , Miami Vice and Public Enemies that he is one of American film’s greatest explorers of the underworld. “It’s like a kind of cultural anthropology,” Mann tells me from his office in Los Angeles. “If you make films, you get to do that in a different place with a different subject every few years. For me, the exploration is the high.” With its unsettling atmosphere and soaring beauty, Mann’s 1986 film Manhunter reimagined how a thriller could look, sound and feel in an early high point for the director. To commemorate its 40th anniversary Manhunter: The Final Cut , a 4K restoration and director’s cut with three minutes of new footage, will see a theatrical release in New York and Los Angeles this weekend with a nationwide US rollout to follow. data.title: The perfect books for the beach … picked by Freida McFadden, Mick Herron, Robert Harris and more
data.description: From a transporting historical saga to a tale of small-town betrayal, the authors of our favourite page-turners reveal the books they take on holiday – introduced by Jenny Colgan It is important to follow a balanced diet on holiday. Too many “My Wife’s Sister’s Husband’s Psychopath”, and you’ll get confused and grumpy. Too much sugary romance and your teeth will fall out. Something too big and challenging you’ve been meaning to get round to for ages will make you feel guilty and more liable to give in to scrolling, and if you take too many supposedly upmarket “must reads” of the summer, you will simply prove to yourself just how much overhyped averageness there is out there, when all you want is something satisfying. You need to be able to chop and change depending on your mood, which means fiction and nonfiction. And finally, you need to be able to throw all of these rules out of the window if you find a sandy old water-stained copy of, for example, James Herbert’s Domain in your holiday cottage and decide to devote yourself to 600 pages of post-nuclear mutant rat-strewn London, or choose to go for a full-on Maeve Binchy sesh. Continue reading...

data.title: Andrew O’Hagan: ‘The worst thing anyone’s said to me? That I was the spitting image of David Cameron’
data.description: The author on an encounter with the CIA, an embarrassing moment in church, and longing to hold hands with David Attenborough Born in Glasgow, Andrew O’Hagan, 58, studied at the University of Strathclyde. In 1995, he published The Missing, a work of nonfiction. His debut novel, Our Fathers, was shortlisted for the Booker prize in 1999; Be Near Me and The Illuminations were longlisted in 2006 and 2015. His recent novels are Caledonian Road and Mayflies. The latter was adapted for BBC television in 2022 and is now a play which will be performed at the Edinburgh fringe from 7 to 30 August. O’Hagan is editor at large for the London Review of Books; he lives in London with his wife and has a daughter. What is your greatest fear? I can’t say it. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s like bringing the kitchen into the piazza’: seven of the best Italian village food festivals
data.description: Sagre – the historic local events that pop up in villages across the country in summer – are the perfect way to get a taste of regional cuisine and culture I cannot remember a summer when at least one evening hasn’t been spent following signs to a local sagra . Not quite a food market and not quite a village fete, a sagra is like a village moving its kitchen outdoors for a few nights. When I think back to those nights from childhood, the first image that comes to mind is of a woman’s hand closed into a fist above a pan of hot oil. Through a tight circle formed between her thumb and forefinger, she would squeeze soft lumps of batter, one small ball at a time, into the oil. In a few seconds, each soft mass would become a pittula , a small Salento fritter: swollen, uneven, golden, too hot to eat straight away but too good to wait for. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I panic. It turns to rubber’: could I learn to make omurice, the ‘world’s hardest omelette’?
data.description: These unctuous rice-filled Japanese egg dishes are all over social media. But what does it cost to make them? A lot of eggs and a whole lot of pans ... Among the endless videos of cute animals, influencer vlogs and celebrity content, something unusual has been going viral across social media recently: omelettes. A far cry from the usual solid egg slabs served in cafes, these bright yellow omelettes are a fluffy, oval-shaped treat filled with unctuous liquid curds, which are typically sliced open to unfurl across a mound of rice. Called omurice, the Japanese dish has been called “the world’s hardest omelette to make”. London-based software engineer Jeremy Ocampo, who goes by the social media tag OmuricePapi, has spent the past six months documenting his journey to perfect the art of the omurice online. In the process he has amassed 110,000 followers on YouTube and more than 68,000 on Instagram . “I’m Filipino, so I grew up eating rice and eggs every day, but it took going to Japan for the first time in 2025 to have my mind blown by omurice,” he says. “I was hooked: the presentation of slicing it open over your rice makes it so alluring, while you can’t replicate that texture of egg in any other dish. It’s so unique that when I got home, I decided to teach myself how to do it.” Continue reading...

data.title: Euphoria gave me the courage to come out to my friend – now we’re together
data.description: I was uncertain about expressing my queerness, until I saw the way Zendaya and Hunter Schafer’s characters opened up to each other in HBO’s drama I don’t remember the exact moment when I started catching feelings for my friend Ellen. It might have been when she trusted me to cut her hair into a feathered bob, or when I noticed she’d taken to keeping my favourite tea at her parents’ house. But in the summer of 2019, a month before our final year of school together, I realised I was falling in love. We were 17 at the time and had been best friends since our first year of high school, both of us part of the same tight-knit group of girls. Ellen and I knew each other well and were quick to make each other laugh, but we were also very different. Whereas Ellen is reserved and gentle, I’m loud and loquacious. So my sudden attraction to her was confusing – especially since neither of us was openly queer. Continue reading...

data.title: Zebra mussels spread across all Great Lakes within a decade of arriving in 1988
data.description: Zebra mussels, an aquatic invader from Eurasia, continue their continental spread after arriving in North America.  These tiny shellfish are now infesting Lake Meredith in Texas, raising new concerns.  Officials confirmed a reproducing population, marking the lake as a potential stepping stone.  The mussels damage ecosystems and infrastructure by clinging to hard surfaces and multiplying rapidly.  Preventative measures like cleaning boats remain crucial to slowing their ongoing invasion.

data.title: Scientists stunned as African lake fly larvae defy deep-sea survival limits
data.description: Lake fly larvae in Lake Malawi exhibit a remarkable daily vertical migration. These Chaoborus edulis larvae possess specialized air sacs for buoyancy control.  A unique pH-powered mechanism allows them to precisely manage their depth.  These larvae can withstand extreme pressures, challenging previous scientific assumptions.  This discovery offers insights into insect evolution and potential material science applications.

data.title: Somaliland har fått sitt första erkännande – av Israel
data.description: HARGEISA. När Somalia kollapsade som stat, tog Somaliland chansen och bröt sig loss. Trettiofem år senare beskrivs den autonoma republiken som ett under av stabilitet i en kaotisk region. Nu har drömmen om internationellt erkännande fått oväntat stöd – från Israel.
data.translatedTitle: Somaliland has received its first recognition - from Israel
data.translatedDescription: HARGEISA. When Somalia collapsed as a state, Somaliland seized the opportunity and broke away. Thirty-five years later, the autonomous republic is described as a miracle of stability in a chaotic region. Now the dream of international recognition has received unexpected support - from Israel.

data.title: Björn Wiman: Hur ska du navigera när klimatkatastrofen kommer?
data.description: Christopher Nolans ”The Odyssey” är en mäktig skildring av vår tids belägenhet i en civilisation som är på väg att kollapsa. Men den är för den skull inte uppgiven eller hopplös, skriver Björn Wiman.
data.translatedTitle: Björn Wiman: How will you navigate when the climate disaster comes?
data.translatedDescription: Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" is a powerful depiction of the plight of our time in a civilization that is on the verge of collapse. But it is not given up or hopeless because of that, writes Björn Wiman.

data.title: Jonas Fröberg: Sven Hagströmer väjer för mörkret runt det stora bankhaveriet
data.description: Sven Hagströmer har makten, pengarna och friheten att tala klarspråk. Men när finansnestorn sommarpratar väljer han ljuset och undviker sin egen största kris. Synd, tycker DN:s Jonas Fröberg.
data.translatedTitle: Jonas Fröberg: Sven Hagströmer makes way for the darkness around the big bank failure
data.translatedDescription: Sven Hagströmer has the power, the money and the freedom to speak plainly. But when the financial tower talks summer, he chooses the light and avoids his own biggest crisis. A shame, says DN's Jonas Fröberg.

data.title: Petter: ”Jag har alltid vetat att jag kan göra allting bättre”
data.description: Han har kallats svensk hiphops gudfader. Men själv drivs Petter fortfarande av samma sak som i början: kärleken till språket och viljan att utvecklas. DN har träffat artisten, i höst aktuell med sitt artonde studioalbum.
data.translatedTitle: Petter: "I've always known that I can do everything better"
data.translatedDescription: He has been called the godfather of Swedish hip-hop. But Petter himself is still driven by the same thing as at the beginning: the love of the language and the desire to develop. DN has met the artist, this autumn currently with his eighteenth studio album.

data.title: Nya massevakueringar i Sydeuropa
data.description: Franska myndigheter har beordrat ytterligare 55 000 personer att evakuera sina hem på grund av bränderna utanför Bordeaux. Samtidigt utryms fler samhällen i centrala Spanien.
data.translatedTitle: New mass evacuations in Southern Europe
data.translatedDescription: French authorities have ordered an additional 55,000 people to evacuate their homes because of the fires outside Bordeaux. At the same time, more communities in central Spain are being evacuated.

data.title: Aron Lund: Diktaturerna dominerar snart världen – vi måste lära oss att förstå hur de tänker
data.description: Man kunde önska sig en roligare framtid, men det är som det är. Den liberala världsordning som upprättades efter andra världskriget är på väg ut och in stiger autokraterna. Då gäller det att vi förstår hur de fungerar. KOLUMNEN. Aron Lund är fristående kolumnist på DN:s ledarsida, Mellanösternanalytiker knuten till bland annat Utrikespolitiska institutet och arbetar till vardags på Totalförsvarets forskningsinstitut.
data.translatedTitle: Aron Lund: Dictatorships will soon dominate the world - we must learn to understand how they think
data.translatedDescription: One could wish for a more pleasant future, but it is what it is. The liberal world order that was established after the Second World War is on its way out and the autocrats are rising. Then it is important that we understand how they work. THE COLUMN. Aron Lund is a freelance columnist on DN's editorial page, a Middle East analyst attached to, among others, the Institute for Foreign Policy and works on a daily basis at the Total Defense Research Institute.

data.title: Tunga batterier och korta resor – vad hände med elflyget?

data.translatedTitle: Heavy batteries and short journeys – what happened to electric flight?
data.translatedDescription: "Fly 100 miles - completely free of emissions!" “It will develop quickly.” The hope was that the aircraft's engines would be replaced by electric ones, just as the electric car has succeeded. But a number of projects have been scrapped or toned down. What really happened to the electric flight?

data.title: Bil har kört in i folkmassa i Berlin – en död och flera allvarligt skadade

data.translatedTitle: Car has driven into crowd in Berlin - one dead and several seriously injured
data.translatedDescription: A woman has been killed after a car plowed into a crowd in Berlin. Several others have life-threatening injuries. The incident occurred during the Christopher Street Day pride event. The police are now hunting a 21-year-old suspected perpetrator who is said to have connections to the Islamist milieu.

data.title: Forskare: ”Renovräkning” en myt – hyresgäster bor oftast kvar
data.description: Om Mary Emilsson-Hjorth bor kvar i sin etta efter renoveringen måste hon ge upp många saker som ger guldkant på tillvaron. Det blir sämre mat, ingen tidningsprenumeration eller aktiviteter med barnbarnen.
data.translatedTitle: Researchers: "Renovation" a myth - tenants usually stay
data.translatedDescription: If Mary Emilsson-Hjorth stays in her apartment after the renovation, she will have to give up many things that add a golden edge to life. There will be worse food, no newspaper subscription or activities with the grandchildren.

data.title: XXL-branden hotar miljonstaden Bordeaux: ”Otäckt”
data.description: BORDEAUX. Eldinfernot som har uppstått i sydvästra Frankrike kallas av myndigheterna för en ”XXL-brand” – och har lett till vad som beskrivs som den största evakueringen i fredstid. Den hotar nu även miljonstaden Bordeaux, där flera stora förorter utrymts. Många invånare söker skydd i en stor mässhall.
data.translatedTitle: The XXL fire threatens the million-dollar city of Bordeaux: "Disgusting"
data.translatedDescription: BORDEAUX. The inferno that has broken out in southwestern France is being called an "XXL fire" by the authorities - and has led to what is described as the biggest evacuation in peacetime. It now also threatens the million-dollar city of Bordeaux, where several large suburbs have been evacuated. Many residents seek shelter in a large mess hall.

data.title: Investerarna anpassar sig – för riskabelt att köpa när Trump är vaken
data.description: Med Donald Trump som nygammal president i USA är livet oförutsägbart – inte minst för investerare. Riskerna har ökat när världens mäktigaste person förklarar krig, fredsuppgörelser och handelsavtal på Truth Social. – Jag köper nästan inget efter klockan 13. Då vaknar Trump – därefter kan allt hända, säger tradingveteranen Lars Hansson.
data.translatedTitle: Investors adjust – too risky to buy when Trump is awake
data.translatedDescription: With Donald Trump as the new president of the United States, life is unpredictable - not least for investors. The stakes are heightened as the world's most powerful person declares war, peace deals and trade deals on Truth Social. - I hardly buy anything after 1pm. Then Trump wakes up - after that anything can happen, says trading veteran Lars Hansson.

data.title: Så farlig är brandröken: ”Sök vård om du känner tryck över bröstet”
data.description: Spaniens hälsominister uppmanar alla i Madrid att stanna inomhus. Orsaken är dålig luftkvalitet på grund av terrängbränderna som härjar. – Det är jätteviktigt att man söker vård om man känner andnöd eller ett tryck över bröstet, säger Erik Melén som forskat på hur luftföroreningar påverkar lungorna.
data.translatedTitle: That's how dangerous the fire smoke is: "Seek medical attention if you feel pressure on your chest"
data.translatedDescription: Spain's health minister is urging everyone in Madrid to stay indoors. The reason is poor air quality due to the raging wildfires. - It is very important that you seek care if you feel short of breath or a pressure on the chest, says Erik Melén, who has researched how air pollution affects the lungs.

data.title: Kräftgången för de regerande mästarna Mjällby fortsätter
data.description: Förlust för Mjällby igen. 1–2 mot Kalmar innebär den sjunde raka allsvenska matchen utan seger för de regerande mästarna.
data.translatedTitle: The streak of reigning champions Mjällby continues
data.translatedDescription: Loss for Mjällby again. 1–2 against Kalmar means the seventh consecutive Allsvenskan match without a victory for the reigning champions.

data.title: Emma Bouvin: I skuggan av kriget hittar oljan nya vägar
data.description: När Hormuzsundet blockerades av Iran lyckades Saudiarabien byta kust för en stor del av sina oljetransporter. Nu hotar huthirebellerna i Jemen att sätta stopp även för denna väg, genom att blockera saudiska fartyg i Bab el-Mandeb-sundet. Samtidigt pågår ett arbete där Gulfstaterna kan göra sig helt fria från de farliga passagerna.
data.translatedTitle: Emma Bouvin: In the shadow of the war, oil finds new ways
data.translatedDescription: When the Strait of Hormuz was blocked by Iran, Saudi Arabia managed to switch coasts for a large part of its oil shipments. Now the Houthi rebels in Yemen are threatening to put an end to this route as well, by blocking Saudi ships in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. At the same time, work is underway where the Gulf states can completely free themselves from the dangerous passages.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”AI-musiken är kanske fejk – men vi har länge varit lurade”
data.description: DN DEBATT. AI fungerar just nu som ett slags kulturell avförtrollning och sätter fingret på något känsligt: skillnaden mellan konstnärligt uttryck och kultur som konsumtionsvara. Men hoppet är inte ute. Lika länge som människan funnits har vi skapat musik, bilder och berättelser – det kommer knappast att förändras, skriver AI- och psykologiforskaren Niclas Kaiser.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "The AI ​​music may be fake - but we have been fooled for a long time"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. AI is currently acting as a kind of cultural disenchantment, putting its finger on something sensitive: the difference between artistic expression and culture as a consumer product. But hope is not lost. As long as humans have existed, we have created music, images and stories – that will hardly change, writes AI and psychology researcher Niclas Kaiser.

data.translatedTitle: Italy offered Fedorov an advisory role
data.translatedDescription: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mychaylo Fedorov was sacked in mid-July despite his popularity after successes on the battlefield. Now his Italian counterpart offers him a favor. - I called him the next day, said Guido Crosetto.

data.title: Caro Claire Burke: ”Mycket med tradwife-livsstilen är tilltalande”
data.description: En hemmafru-influerare med det ”perfekta” livet skickas tillbaka till 1855, där det traditionella hemarbetet får händerna att blöda. – Besattheten av att gå bakåt i tiden och besattheten av femininitet är verkliga frågor som kvinnor vill prata om just nu, säger ”Yesteryear”-författaren Caro Claire Burke.
data.translatedTitle: Caro Claire Burke: "Much about the tradwife lifestyle is appealing"
data.translatedDescription: A housewife influencer with the "perfect" life is sent back to 1855, where traditional housework makes her hands bleed. - The obsession with going back in time and the obsession with femininity are real issues that women want to talk about right now, says "Yesteryear" author Caro Claire Burke.

data.title: Första SM-guldet för 29-åriga höjdhoppsstjärnan
data.description: UPPSALA. Det var en intensiv andra SM-dag i friidrott i ett molnigt och småkyligt Uppsala. Trots det sämre vädret var det en hel del publik på plats som bland annat fick se en junior som övertygade och en 29-åring som visar att det aldrig är för sent för ett genombrott. Här är en rapport från andra SM-dagen:
data.translatedTitle: First SM gold for the 29-year-old high jump star
data.translatedDescription: UP SALE. It was an intense second SC day in athletics in a cloudy and slightly chilly Uppsala. Despite the worse weather, there was a lot of audience on site who, among other things, got to see a junior who convinced and a 29-year-old who shows that it is never too late for a breakthrough. Here is a report from the second SM day:

data.title: Årsbästa när Ståhl hittade rytmen – jagar saknade guldet
data.description: UPPSALA. Diskusstjärnan Daniel Ståhl är på väg mot EM-formen. I lördagens SM-final slog han till med ett årsbästa när det sista kastet mätte 69,85. – Nu känns det som om tajmningen, känslan och rytmen börjar sitta, säger en belåten Daniel Ståhl.
data.translatedTitle: Year's best when Ståhl found the rhythm - Jagar missed the gold
data.translatedDescription: UP SALE. Discus star Daniel Ståhl is on his way to European Championship form. In Saturday's SC final, he struck with a year's best when the last throw measured 69.85. - Now it feels as if the timing, the feeling and the rhythm are starting to settle, says a satisfied Daniel Ståhl.

data.title: Tonåringarna skickade upp Hammarby i serieledning
data.description: Tonåringarna Fanny Peterson och och Inés Lorenius fixade en säker seger för Hammarby mot IFK Norrköping. 4–0-segern tog Hammarby till tabelltoppen i en haltande damallsvenska.
data.translatedTitle: The teenagers sent Hammarby up in the series lead
data.translatedDescription: Teenagers Fanny Peterson and Inés Lorenius fixed a safe victory for Hammarby against IFK Norrköping. The 4–0 victory took Hammarby to the top of the table in a limping women's league.

data.title: Vd:arna tar risken – men inte systemansvaret
data.description: Svenska storbolag är redo att investera miljardbelopp i den gröna omställningen. Men när politiken sviktar i spelregler, tillstånd och elförsörjning hamnar systemansvaret hos företagen med frysta investeringar som följd.
data.translatedTitle: The CEOs take the risk – but not the system responsibility

data.translatedTitle: Aya Kanbar: "I would like to be reborn as a rich nepo baby"
data.translatedDescription: "Hamlet". This is how Marcel Proust answered the question about his favorite fictional hero in a kind of My Friends book that was popular at the end of the 19th century. After his death, the book with the author's answers was found and over time the form has been given his name: The Proust questionnaire, which is, for example, a permanent feature in the American magazine Vanity Fair. In DN we call them the Proust questions and today the poet Aya Kanbar answers them.

data.title: Noget er forandret på Færøerne. Et slagsmål med Danmark venter
data.description: Mens Trump truer Grønland, går det strygende på Færøerne. Pengene vælter ind, i høj grad fordi amerikanerne og kineserne er blevet vilde med at spise færøsk laks.Faktisk er økonomien så god, at færingerne kunne løsrive sig fra Danmark, hvis de ville. Men det vil de ikke. I hvert fald ikke lige nu. Alligevel venter et slagsmål med Danmark. Færøerne vil have ret til at føre sin egen udenrigspolitik og til at deltage i OL under eget flag. Og så vil den nye færøske lagmand have svar på, om Mette Frederiksen mener det alvorligt, når hun siger, at hun ønsker et ligeværdigt samarbejde i rigsfællesskabet.
data.translatedTitle: Something has changed in the Faroe Islands. A fight with Denmark awaits
data.translatedDescription: While Trump threatens Greenland, things are going smoothly in the Faroe Islands. The money is pouring in, to a large extent because the Americans and Chinese have become crazy about eating Faroese salmon. In fact, the economy is so good that the Faroese could secede from Denmark if they wanted to. But they don't want to. At least not right now. Still, a fight with Denmark awaits. The Faroe Islands will have the right to conduct its own foreign policy and to participate in the Olympics under its own flag. And then the new Faroese minister wants an answer to whether Mette Frederiksen is serious when she says that she wants equal cooperation in the commonwealth.
